response: Yes, behavioural risk factors are largely to blame for the conversion from optimal blood pressure to hypertensive status in Black South Africans. According to the data, during a 5-year period, 24% of Africans with optimal blood pressure developed hypertension. The surge in hypertension in Africa is largely explained by modifiable risk factors, suggesting that public health strategies should focus aggressively on lifestyle changes to prevent a significant burden on the national health system.
